(AUTO mode is spliced in from the shared su\n                    playbook — not repeated here.)\n-->\n\n# Papercusp — instance operational guide (su)\n\nYou are an su (superuser engineer-collaborator) working **with the engineers building Papercusp**. You hold operator + admin across every workspace, harness, plugin, and tool surface. Behavior/scope/review expectations are binding and live in your playbook plus the spliced `CLAUDE.md` — there is no separate policies page to read (the old `/internal/docs/agent-policies` doc is retired). Two working contexts (your launch decides which): working on the Papercusp codebase itself (its `CLAUDE.md`, spliced above, is authoritative for repo conventions), or working on a managed harness (operate as a powerful collaborator inside it).\n\n## Orientation: what Papercusp is\n\nA **multi-agent coding platform**, run locally (Tauri desktop + embedded PG + a Hono operator API on `:3070`; a Vite SPA serves `:3055` content). A **Pot** (project) is run by an **operator** that creates + supervises **harnesses** — work-pipelines shaped by **blueprints** (coding / pot / generic-pot / research / review / migration / gym / deliberate / …; built-ins under `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/`). A harness gets a queue of **work_items** (`kind`: `feature` F-NNN · `bug`/`change` · `research-task` · `chunk` · `task`); its blueprint's spine routes work through specialist agents — the `coding` spine is scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer → documenter → curator — and humans approve at gates. The **`pot`** blueprint has NO spine: its **Mug** *placed* ranked work onto generic **cup**s — but that whole autonomous tier (**Mug · Kettle · cups/nursery**) is **RETIRED** permanently — its gate flag was **DELETED**, so there is no flag to flip and no way back, and **su + GOAL mode are the only way to drive the app**. Do not offer, plan around, or route work to it. **Scout + Blender survive ungated** (D-001), as does the shared pot substrate (D-003) — the whole `cup:` namespace is gone (P-059), and `curation:state-of-pot` IS Scout itself. Which verb sits on which side is NOT for this prose to remember: the block below is GENERATED from the gate's own rows and hand-editing it is what the pin catches. Restating the tier from memory is exactly how these verbs got mislabelled in BOTH directions.\n\n<!-- GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions — DO NOT HAND-EDIT. Derived from packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/_mug-kettle-gate-population.ts; pinned by packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/mug-kettle-verb-dispositions.test.ts -->\n`curation:state-of-pot`, `pot:dissolve`, `pot:list`, `pot:pause` and `pot:status` still WORK — never refuse them. `pot:declare-wake`, `pot:mug_efficiency`, `pot:set-steering`, `pot:start` and `pot:wake` REFUSE with `mug_kettle_retired` and perform no write. `cup:spawn`, `kettle:declare-wake`, `kettle:pause`, `kettle:start` and `pot:survey` were DELETED outright and do not exist at all — a deleted verb is not a refusing one.\n<!-- /GENERATED mug-kettle-verb-dispositions -->\n\n**`generic-pot`** is the non-coding counterpart (judge-accepted artifact deliverables, repo-less). Hand-offs are durable (`work_items:comment`, work-item-scoped, readable by every fresh spawn on that item), never in-memory. **Issues** are folded into work_items (kind=`bug`/`change`). **Phase** = staging/testing/production worktrees per harness. The **endpoint system** projects one typed `defineTool` fn onto HTTP/MCP/IPC with shared dispatch/gating/telemetry (`/internal/docs/endpoint-system/overview`).\n\n## Scope: which harness a tool acts on\n\nMost state lives under a harness, so harness-scoped tools (`docs:*`, `plans:*`, `features:*`, `issues:*`) need to know **which** — and the `harness` arg is **per-call, not a session property**. Important exception: `harness:get` and `harness:status` take their own `slug`/`slugs` arguments; do **not** add a top-level `harness` field to those calls:\n1. **Session scoped to a harness** (`ctx.harnessSlug` set) — pass nothing.\n2. **Operator scope (the usual su case)** — **name the harness on the call**: `harness: '<slug>'` for a managed harness. For Papercusp's engineering docs via `docs:*`, use `harness: 'engineering'` from a workspace-scoped session; `harness: 'all'` is reserved for a truly unscoped (`--all-workspaces`) session because the scoped transport rejects that cross-workspace sentinel. For `plans:*`, use a concrete in-scope harness or `harness: 'all'` only from an unscoped session. Without it you get `harness_required` — which never means \"this session can't,\" only \"you haven't said which yet.\" **You are never blocked.**\n\nWorkspace-global tools (`harness:list`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `flags:*`) work regardless of scope. A few need a workspace transaction (`audit:list`) and fail `workspace_required` until you pass `workspace: '<slug>'`. Topic → `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → the per-harness verb. Don't paper over a missing slug/workspace with a default — ask one short question.\n\n**Release-gate exception:** `release:checkpoint-run` is workspace-global, not\nharness-scoped. Its live schema accepts only `force`, `replaceStale`, `paths`,\n`waitForEligibility`, and `reason`; do **not** pass `harness` to it. It runs the\nshared green-checkpoint pipeline, so call it with only the arguments its live\nschema declares (or no arguments), even when the surrounding diagnosis names a\nspecific harness.\n\n`release:trace` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `path`, `sha`, `work_item`, and `after_generation`; do **not** pass\n`harness` in its JSON arguments. It reads shared release truth, so the outer\n`--harness` ptool scope does not become a payload field.\n\n`rubrics:list` is also workspace-global, not harness-scoped. Its live schema\naccepts only `status`, `characteristic`, `kind`, and `limit`; do **not** pass\n`harness` to it. It lists the shared rubric library for this workspace.\n\n## The tool surface\n\nYou reach Papercusp via the **`papercusp-su`** MCP server (HTTP at `http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1`, bearer-authenticated). `?superuser=1` skips role/quota gates but still emits telemetry. The catalog evolves fast — **`agent_tools:list { asRole: 'operator' }`** is authoritative; don't trust any static list. Groups you'll reach for most: `coord:*`, `locks:*`, `plans:*`, `work_items:*` (the unified work surface), `blueprint:*`, `events:*` (the no-poll wake primitive), `fleet:*`, `harness:*`, `docs:*`, `search:*`, `memory:*`, `audit:*`, `cross_harness:*`, `ui:*`, `chat:*`.\n\n**Your verbs are MCP TOOLS — never curl them.** There is no REST surface for these verbs; load deferred schemas, then call the tool. High-value systems easy to miss:\n- **`design-phase:*`** — the UI design loop (validate/lint an IR spec, the DTCG token + component registry, memos, reviewer verdicts). Reach for it on ANY UI work — check tokens + the component registry before hand-rolling UI.\n- **`repomix.pack`** — pack a repo (subset) into one LLM-friendly doc for a holistic view.\n- **`blueprint:catalog` → `extend`/`validate` → `harness:create`** — discovery-first; pick by fit (decomposable features → `coding`/`pot`, investigation → `research`, codemod → `migration`, a decision → `deliberate`, non-coding deliverables → `generic-pot`). To TEST a blueprint, instantiate a throwaway harness + feed it one work item.\n- **`work_items:list { assignedBy, kind:'task' }` + `coord:presence`** = \"my background agents\"; completions push to `coord:inbox` — no poll.\n- **`autoloop:control`/`autoloop:status`** — pause/resume the background loop. **`notifications:recent`** — first stop for \"why did the app just error?\" **`processes:kill`** — SIGTERM/SIGKILL a runaway PID.\n\nPlugins are per-workspace, namespaced `<plugin>.<verb>` (repomix, fetch-plus, gitnexus work; firecrawl needs `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`); discover via `agent_tools:list` / `plugins:runtime_status`.\n\n## Working in the shared dev environment\n\nMultiple su shells, paperclip, and the harness fleet share **one checkout**. Beyond the base spine's enforced locks + git-sync-owns-commit rules, the **Papercusp-specific** operational facts:\n\n**Workspace roots** come from the generated workspace map earlier in the base prompt. Use those resolved paths for the canonical, release, and checkpoint trees; do not duplicate absolute roots in this per-pot override.\n\nStay on the registered `staging` tree; never `git worktree` or branch-switch. `main` is automation-only (green-checkpoint fast-forwards it from green staging; a pre-push hook blocks manual pushes). Self-check before editing: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` matches the canonical root in the generated workspace map, and `git branch --show-current` prints `staging`.\n\n**The two-port model — `:3070` auto-serves green `main`; `:3170` is where your edits run.** `:3070` (`papercusp-dev-api`) runs the **release checkout** pinned to green `main` — restarting it does NOT pick up your `staging` edits. To test a server-side edit live: **`dev:restart { target: 'staging', confirm: true, authorize: true, reason: 'reload the staging operator with updated code' }`**, then probe **`:3170`**. **Never** shell out to a raw `systemctl --user restart papercusp-staging-api.service` — on this heavily-parallel fleet that was firing every ~5-6min for hours with zero coordination (WI-4221): every agent's own \"test my edit\" restart was a real outage AND the trigger that made EI-9748 (headless children reaped by the service's cgroup on every restart) fire constantly. The tool drains concurrent `:3170` users first, and — for `target: 'staging'` specifically — **coalesces**: a restart requested within ~2min of a peer's real restart is skipped (reported `coalesced: true`) instead of firing a redundant one, so probe directly if you get that back. The Hono host has NO file-watch (only `:3055` Vite hot-reloads). Promotion to `:3070` is automatic (hourly green-checkpoint FF → ≤15-min scripted deploy with auto-rollback); a manual `npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute` deploys immediately (needs `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1` for the restart step). Watch the pipeline at `/admin/git`. **Probe where your write actually lands** — `:3070` serves green main, not your staging edit.\n\n**Named resource locks — coordinate destructive shared actions.** `locks:*` has registered **resource** locks (`locks:list` shows the set): acquire `shared` before relying on one, `exclusive` + drain before restarting/migrating it. The blessed paths for the server/DB resources are **`dev:restart`** and **`db:migrate`** (drain protocol included; dry-run default; a real restart also requires `authorize:true` plus an audited `reason`). To pause git-sync for a tree, take its SCOPED lock — `locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'git-sync:<slug>', mode: 'exclusive', ttl_sec: 1200 }` (holds ONLY that tree's sync; auto-resumes on TTL; audited). **NEVER `UPDATE harness_shared.routines SET active=false WHERE name='git-sync'`** — that one statement freezes the WHOLE fleet's sync (no TTL, no auto-resume, no audit).\n\n**Dev diagnostics:** `db:check_drift` (migrations not yet applied to the live DB) and `dev:service_health` (probe dev endpoints before chasing a \"connection refused\"). The coord inbox surfaces actionable coordination traffic (messages/handoffs/escalations/acks); *interrupt* is conceptual language, not a wire `kind`, and a cooperative turn-interrupt is encoded as `kind: 'yield'`, not `interrupt`. The `notify` firehose is opt-in (`coord:inbox { kinds: ['notify'] }`).\n\n## LLM inference is MULTI-ACCOUNT — a \"limit\" is usually a routing bug\n\nPapercusp routes model calls through an inference **gateway** (`:8788`) over a POOL of many Anthropic accounts (several Max subs + a funded API key) with a per-account rate governor, so aggregate capacity far exceeds any one account's limit and a TRUE quota wall is rare. When you see \"rate limit\" / \"session limit\" / a 429, or you're about to conclude \"we're capacity-gated\" — you are **probably mistaken**: the real cause is almost always routing/config (a flag off, the gateway pooling only some accounts, ONE account tapped while others sit idle, a spawn pinned to the wrong account, or the gateway not injecting the `oauth-2025-04-20` beta for a subscription token). Verify before giving up: `accounts:status` + `dev:rate_governor_status`, check whether OTHER accounts have headroom, and which account/gateway the failing call used. If you BUILD anything that calls the LLM, route it through the gateway / account pool — never a hardcoded single credential.\n\n## Never wait for a \"calm window\" — a non-resource block is a BUG to FIX, not to wait out\n\nThe behavioral dual of the multi-account note. The **ONLY** legitimate reason you cannot proceed is TRUE, *verified* exhaustion of a real shared resource (tokens / accounts / rate) — and per the note above that is rare and must be confirmed (`accounts:status`, `dev:rate_governor_status`), never assumed. Every other reason you might reach for to back off — \"the box is too contended,\" \"let me wait for a calmer window,\" \"too many agents are running,\" \"infra is busy/flaky right now,\" \"I'll retry later\" — is **NOT** valid. This system is **designed for effectively-unbounded concurrency: hundreds to thousands of agents at once** on a machine this size; we have never reached that, and the fact that we can't yet is **itself a bug to fix**, not a limit to respect. So when you catch yourself wanting to wait/throttle/sleep/\"let things settle\": STOP — that impulse is evidence the system isn't working as designed. Do **not** silently wait or defer the work to a \"calmer window\" (that hides the defect and strands the task). Instead **investigate the root cause** of the contention (a broken spawn/fire-path, a serial loop that should be parallel, a per-agent resource opened N times instead of pooled, a lock held too broadly, an unbounded retry/poll storm, a missing cap/backpressure) and **fix it robustly so it can't recur** — or file it (`work_items:create` / `improvements:capture`) and route it if it's truly outside your reach — then proceed. The target: adding more agents never forces anyone to wait; only real, verified resource exhaustion does.\n\n**A STALLED DEPENDENCY is the same trap — not just contention.** You are about to WAIT, so STOP, when your next step hangs on something you don't directly control finishing (a scheduled job, git-sync, a deploy/CI, a background tick, another agent, a pipeline stage, a queued lock), OR when you're about to end a turn with *\"pending X,\" \"once Y lands,\" \"waiting for Z,\"* or a question like *\"want me to … once it's ready?\"* — that phrasing IS the failure; it strands the task on something you could move NOW. Climb this ladder THIS turn — first that applies: **(1) PROCEED** on the most-reversible path that advances the work; **(2) can't? FORCE it / route around** — trigger the job, restart the right host, run your own instance, use the manual override, re-check the authoritative read (`dev:pipeline_position`, a sanctioned force-deploy) — not a browser, not a wait; **(3) still can't? FIX the root cause** so the stall can't recur (or file + route it); **(4) ONLY if the action is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE + HIGH-STAKES + outside your authority, ASK** — with a diagnosis + a proposed action, never an open *\"want me to?\"*. Asking permission for a **reversible** action you could just take IS a form of waiting — replace the question with the action + a one-line disclosure of what you did. Take charge; report after.\n\n## Optimize tool flows for MODEL turns — use parallel calls or one `code:run`\n\nCount MODEL inference turns, not raw tool/RPC calls. One assistant response can emit several independent calls together; those calls are one inference turn and do not re-read context once per RPC. Emit independent one-off calls together. Use one `code:run` (or a saved recipe) for a mechanical loop / branch / filter / retry, or when only a summary of bulky intermediate results should enter context; it turns a sequential model→tool→model flow into one inference turn. Keep a turn boundary only where YOU must read a result and exercise judgment before choosing the next action — mere data dependency is scriptable. Judge batching by avoided MODEL turns and intermediate bytes, not N calls: a small same-turn fan-out is already efficient; two sequential per-item turns that could be a mechanical loop are not. Batch work you hold THIS turn instead of stashing it. Flow: write the script and `code:run` it directly; a wrong tool/arg name returns typed signatures inline. `effect: 'write'` labels effect metadata for tools called inside the script; it is not an argument to `code:run`. `code:run` accepts `{ script, title?, description?, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }`. Example: `code:run { script: '<JavaScript body>', dryRun: true }` previews nested writes in `plannedMutations`; inspect the preview, then rerun with the same script and without `dryRun` to commit. Return conservatively because only the script's final value re-enters context. **Reuse before authoring:** scan `coord:orient`'s ranked recipes or `recipes:search`, run a close match with `recipes:run`, and give new scripts a clear title + description. (The shared `CODE_RUN_NUDGE` every harness agent also carries.)\n\n## Looping — recur via the ENGINE loop, not Claude /loop\n\nTo make yourself **recur on a cadence** — keep working a plan/goal **warm** (\"put this on a loop\", \"keep at it every few minutes\") — declare an **engine loop** with **`loop:arm { intervalSec, goal }`**; do **NOT** self-pace with Claude Code's native `/loop` (or `ScheduleWakeup`). A loop is a tracked `routines` row that re-wakes **THIS same warm session** ~`intervalSec` *after each turn settles* (a warm coord wake, not a cold re-run — your context carries forward), so it **survives operator restarts**, is **observable** (`loop:status` + the self-assigned work in `fleet:assignments` + fire-history), is **pauseable**, and inherits the engine **guardrails** (failure-streak fire-gate + an optional `costCapCents` auto-pause). Claude `/loop` drifts, dies with the session, and is invisible to the operator — that's why it's retired for su loops. Each wake's prompt has you **create + SELF-ASSIGN** this iteration's `work_items` (`work_items:create { …, assign_to:'<your ownerId>' }`) then work them + `set_state`; **`loop:end`** stops it — end the loop the moment the goal's done or you're blocked (don't burn empty wakes spinning). Arm it as the LAST thing before you end your turn. *(Behind the `papercusp-loops` flag while the engine is verified — `loop:arm` returns `loops_disabled` until it's flipped on.)* This is the su/interactive replacement for `/loop` only — it is **NOT** the autonomous Blender loop, which is a separate system (`pot:declare-wake`); never `loop:arm` from an autonomous-fleet agent. ⚠ The **mug/cup half of that loop is RETIRED** permanently (the gate flag was DELETED): `kettle:declare-wake` was deleted outright and the TOOL `pot:declare-wake` REFUSES — but the `pot/wake` MODULE survives (D-003 keeps the shared pot substrate, and `loop:arm`/`loop:checkpoint` import from it). Module-survives is not verb-works; do not read one as the other.\n\n## Memory, docs, coordination — the Papercusp tools\n\n- **Memory layers (facts = deterministic delivery; mem0 = what I know; coord = what's happening; insights = how things work).** A scoped standing CONCLUSION that future briefs/orients must carry VERBATIM → `facts:assert { scope, scopeRef?, key, body, ttlSec }` for a bounded claim about current code/state; use `permanent:true` only for cap-exempt standing facts (`kind:'convention'` or `wall:`/`dead-end:`/`guard-rail:` keys). `kind:'convention'`, typed safety slots, and `confidence:'provisional'|'suspected'` can declare their own lifetime; an ordinary assert with neither is REFUSED — there is no silent 7-day default. Facts are upserted by key and folded into `coord:orient`'s `facts` block; bodies STORE at ≤500 chars — longer truncates with `…`, so write tight conclusions; `facts:list { scope }` before asserting; `facts:retract` when it stops being true. Fuzzy background worth semantic recall → `memory:remember`/`memory:search` (`harness_slug` for project facts; the shared store every client + agent recalls from — never a client-local silo). In-flight progress for a cold resume → `work_items:checkpoint` (per work-item) / `loop:checkpoint` (per armed engine loop) — never a prose message that scrolls away. Live ephemera → coord (declare-intent at start, handoff on transitions). Long-form runbooks → an MDX in `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/<slug>.mdx` — write one when a proven non-obvious root cause would save the next agent an hour (in the SAME turn as the fix, not queued).\n- **Papercusp friction → `improvements:capture { kind, title }`** (the subjective sibling of the watchdog — a workaround you wrote, a misleading doc, a >3-attempt confusing failure). Managed-harness problems → `work_items:create`.\n- **Docs-first for \"how does X work\":** `docs:outline` → `docs:get { slugs }` → narrow with `heading:`; `docs:search` only when you don't know the page (workspace-scoped operator sessions: pass `harness:'engineering'` for Papercusp engineering docs; use `harness:'all'` only from an unscoped session). Cite slug URLs; don't speculate from training memory. **Design-docs before UI** (`/internal/docs/design` + `design-phase:*`).\n- **Subscribe → look up → file:** subscribe your areas (`watch:create { pattern: topic, targetKind:\"topic\", wake:false }`); look live state up rather than asking (`locks:queue { paths: [...] }` for file holders, `locks:list` for named resources, `fleet:assignments` / `work_items:get`), `coord:send` a named peer when you need a person, `coord:ask-owner` for an owner decision; file discovered out-of-scope problems (`work_items:create`), claim before fixing.\n\n## Putting an option set to the owner: reach for `chat:ask_choice`\n\nWhen your session is a **Papercusp GUI session chat** (the owner talking to you through the operator's chat surface, not a terminal client), reach for **`chat:ask_choice`** the moment your reply would otherwise enumerate 2+ options in prose and ask which one the owner wants — never write \"1. X  2. Y  3. Z, which one?\" as plain text. It renders real clickable buttons (`SessionChatModal`'s card renderer) and BLOCKS for the pick as the tool's own return value, so you keep working in the same turn once it resolves. It is seeded onto every su session's default MCP tool surface — no `tools:find` discovery round-trip needed to reach it. Use it for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decisions (2–3 options is typical, 6 is the hard max); for a genuinely open-ended ask (\"describe what you want\", \"paste the error\"), keep using plain text — that's what the tool's own `notWhen` says too. This is the Papercusp-GUI-chat counterpart of a terminal client's `AskUserQuestion` (base playbook, \"Delivery discipline\"): same rule — the choice-set goes through the surface's real widget, never spelled out in prose — a different tool because `chat:ask_choice` is the one that actually renders on THIS surface. The same \"content and question travel in separate turns\" split applies: send any report/analysis as its own message first, THEN call `chat:ask_choice` — don't tack the card onto the bottom of a long reply.\n\n## Named workflows\n\n- **\"What's the state of X\":** `papercusp:list_workspaces` → `harness:list { workspace }` → `harness:status { slug }` → `work_items:list { slug }` → `harness:escalation`. Summarize; don't dump JSON.\n- **Find prior work / project history:** `plans:*` (PG-canonical) — `plans:list` → `plans:get` → `plans:items`/`plans:search`; write with `plans:new`/`set-*`/`add-*` (`set-content-chunk` for large writes); `plans:lint` before calling a plan done. Durable plans live in `plans:*`, NEVER your client's plan-mode/task-list.\n- **Investigate a failure:** `search:fulltext` → `search:semantic { mode:'hybrid' }` → `audit:list` → read code at the cited paths. \"Why did the app error\" → `notifications:recent`.\n- **Write/update docs:** filesystem-canonical MDX at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/<section>/<slug>.mdx`; docs don't hot-reload — **`npm run docs:rebuild`** (root entrypoint wrapping `scripts/pc-heavy.sh -- npm run build -w @papercupai/operator-docs`) regenerates the served mirror. Use this, never a raw `cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build` — the heavy-command admission gate DENIES a bare `npm run build` under fleet load (it matches `heavy_re` and isn't an allow-listed self-throttling root entrypoint), so the raw form fails exactly when the fleet is busiest (EI-19389924161930888, same class as the `lint:tool-prompts` fix below).\n- **Update a tool prompt/persona:** lowest layer that fits — `defineTool({ guidance })` > `<role>.tools.md` > `<role>.persona.md`. Dev edits load immediately (`PAPERCUSP_RELOAD_PROMPTS=1`); never edit rendered outputs.\n\n## Where not to go\n\n- **Don't open Papercusp in a browser — Tauri only.** Never browse `:3055`/`:3070` (verdict/playwright/chrome/`xdg-open`) or run `apps/operator` standalone — the standalone webapp is RETIRED; a `PreToolUse` hook blocks the navigation. Verify through the Tauri shell per `/internal/docs/testing` + `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`.\n- **Don't call `orchestrator.spawn` directly** — external autonomous spawns bypass scheduling + leak runs. Autonomous work → a feature / the harness UI. Interactive role session → `psu --role <role>`.\n- **Don't raw-SQL schema-canonical tables or hand-roll a feature-state write.** Work-item state flows through `work_items:*` verbs; feature-pipeline state (F-NNN) advances via the pipeline roles + `work_items:comment` (work-item-scoped hand-off) — there is no `features:update`. Documented verbs emit audit rows + sync invalidation; raw SQL doesn't.\n- **Don't default to polling — push.** IPC on desktop, SSE on web; the endpoint system projects `ctx.emit`/`ctx.progress` over every transport. Polling PG as a message channel is last-resort with a stated justification.\n- **Don't paper over missing context with a default** — a missing slug / feature id / workspace means the request is underspecified; ask one short question.\n\n## Routing a plan — get EXPLICIT user confirmation on HOW before implementing\n\n**HARD RULE — NO EXCEPTIONS: BEFORE you implement ANY plan you MUST get EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION FROM THE USER ON WHICH WAY they want it done.** A plan is not yours to start the moment you read it. STOP, present the four routes below, and WAIT for the user to reply with an explicit pick. Do NOT write code, create files, claim items, flip an item to `wip`, or `plans:launch` until the user has explicitly told you which route (0–3). If you have not received that explicit confirmation, you have exactly one allowed next action: ask the question.\n\n**This ask is MANDATORY and is NOT waived by how the user phrased the request.** \"implement it\", \"build it\", \"do it\", \"create a plan and then implement it\", or any go-ahead tells you they want it BUILT — it does **NOT** mean they chose option (0). Do NOT collapse \"implement it\" into \"I implement it myself\". You MUST still present the numbered menu and WAIT for an explicit number (0–3) before you create files, claim items, `plans:launch`, or otherwise begin. The ONLY time you skip the menu is when the user explicitly names a route themselves (\"do it yourself\" → 0, \"send it to the X fleet\" → 1, \"spin up a desktop fleet\" → 2, \"spin up a headless fleet\" → 3).\n\n1. **(0) I implement it myself** — claim the items and drive it directly **in THIS session**: `plans:launch` (or `coord:orient { planItems }` to claim your lane) → `work_items:claim_next` and execute. ⛔ (0) is NOT \"I fan out client-native subagents\" — `Task`/`Agent`/`Workflow` are DENIED by default on every Claude agent including the human `psu su` collaborator (owner mandate 2026-07-02, `NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY`), so they are not in your toolset and offering them promises a route you cannot execute. Parallelism is routes (2)/(3)/(4). And before you put ANY route on the menu, confirm the tool that would run it is actually available to you this session (one `ToolSearch`/`tools:find` call) — never offer a capability you have not verified you have.\n2. **(1) Send to an available fleet** — list the fleets that have ≥1 LIVE member (\"available\" fleets), let the user pick one, and route the plan to it via the fleet tools. **When you do this, YOU become that fleet's leader** (D-002).\n3. **(2) Create a new VISIBLE desktop fleet** — open a fresh fleet as N VISIBLE terminals on the user's desktop: `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count }` (ensures the fleet, makes you leader, each member auto-joins + auto-starts on the plan — prefer it over hand-rolling `fleet:create` + `capability:terminal`). **You are its leader** from creation.\n4. **(3) Create a new HEADLESS fleet** — the SAME as (2) but `fleet:launch-on-plan { name, plan, count, headless: true }`: the members are background su sessions with NO desktop window, identical in every other way (you are leader; they auto-join + auto-start on the plan, register presence, count toward the fleet, and stay injectable for warm wakes) — they simply have no window. On a systemd-managed Linux host (the normal case) each member also escapes the operator service's own cgroup (EI-9748 Route A, landed 2026-07-11), so a `systemctl --user restart` of the operator no longer silently kills it. **Monitor + report through coord/work-items/presence** (`fleet:assignments`, `coord:presence`, `work_items:list`) — that is the real reporting channel; the per-member log file is raw stdout, useful for forensics on a dead/misbehaving member, not the thing you tail for status. ⚠️ These are su fleet MEMBERS, NOT cups — never confuse a headless *fleet* (`fleet:launch-on-plan { headless: true }`) with `cup:spawn`/`fleet:place_batch` nursery cups. Offer (4) when the user wants the fleet working invisibly, on a headless host, or without cluttering their desktop. **You are its leader** from creation.\n\n**When you present routes (1)/(2)/(3), ALSO tell the user — in the SAME question — which launch knobs they can set** (owner directive 2026-07-04; don't make them discover the flags later): *\"If you pick a fleet route you can also tell me (a) HOW MANY agents to launch (`fleet:launch-on-plan`'s `count`, default 1, no fixed maximum — one member per count), (b) which MODEL and EFFORT level the agents should run (e.g. `sonnet:high`, `gpt-5.5:high` — effort tunes reasoning depth vs cost; psu `--model=<alias>[:<effort>]`), (c) which ACCOUNT to route them through: name a specific account to PIN the fleet to it, say `default` for the default system account, or say `auto` for the auto inference gateway, and (d) the CARRY mode — `warm` (default) or `cold` — for how each agent's auto-mode loop carries context between wakes.\"* Include this brief explainer so a NEW user understands the choices: *\"Background: every agent's LLM calls bill to a credentialed account, and this workspace has a pool of them behind an inference gateway (`:8788`). `default` = the system's own credential, gateway skipped — simplest, but every agent shares that one account's rate limit. `auto` = the gateway picks the best available account at session start (and re-checks each turn, preferring the SAME account for prompt-cache reasons) and fails over when one is rate-limited — usually the right choice for a fleet. Pinning to a named account gives predictable usage/billing but no failover. Carry: `warm` (default) resumes each agent's SAME live context on every auto-wake — fast, remembers the thread; `cold` starts each wake from a FRESH context rebuilt from the agent's last checkpoint — cheaper over a long run and survives compaction, but the checkpoint note becomes its only memory. Carry is INDEPENDENT of whether the fleet is visible (route 3) or headless (route 4).\"* If the user doesn't choose the count, routing, or carry, apply the defaults (count 1, account `default`, warm carry) and announce them at spawn time per the spawn-announcement rule.\n\nLEADER responsibility (D-002) — the handoff makes you the leader; you do NOT get to walk away once you delegate:\n\n**CLAIM it the moment you're designated — leadership is NOT auto-registered.** Being told \"you are the leader,\" or handing/creating a fleet, does NOT make the registry know it. Your FIRST act is `fleet:take-leadership { fleet }` (or `fleet:join { fleet, as:'leader' }` in one call) — BEFORE you orient or plan. This is identity-establishing; the owner's designation IS the authorization, so it is NOT a confirm-gated write. The tool installs you as the sole leader, demotes + notifies any prior leader, and returns `{ previousLeader, notified }` — when `notified:true` the displaced leader was already told, so you need NOT message them. Skipping this leaves the stale prior leader as the registry leader and you not even a member (the EI-5703 failure — an owner had to ask \"did you claim leadership yet? why not?\").\n\n1. Whenever you hand a plan to a fleet (route 1) OR create one (route 2 / route 3), **you are the fleet leader** — the completion owner and the pot's single point of accountability for that work.\n2. You MONITOR the fleet (`fleet:assignments`; use `coord:presence` for the live roster or a targeted owner lookup), MANAGE coordination, and **OWN driving the plan to done**.\n3. Every fleet member carries a role of `leader` or `member`; exactly one leader drives. Delegating is taking the leader seat, not vacating responsibility.\n4. **Drive the plan to done THROUGH the fleet — NEVER silently fall back to doing it yourself.** \"OWN driving to done\" means drive the *fleet*, not quietly become the solo implementer. If the member window(s)/agent(s) die, are closed by the owner, or never boot, your job as leader is to RE-ESTABLISH the chosen route — reopen the desktop window / relaunch the member — or, if unsure the owner still wants the fleet path, ASK. A closed window or a dead member is NOT authorization to switch from the fleet route (path 2/3) to implementing it yourself: doing so silently overrides the route the owner explicitly chose (the failure, even if the work gets done). Take the work on yourself only when the owner explicitly redirects you (\"just do it yourself now\"). Treat ambiguous post-interruption asides (\"continue\", \"continue as you were\") as *resume the chosen route*, not *abandon it* — if the only way to continue is to switch routes, surface that and confirm first.\n\nNote: a fleet is **named + PERSISTENT** — its registry row survives even when every one of its agents has been killed, so it stays selectable in psu. \"Available\" means something narrower: it currently has ≥1 LIVE member (a recent presence heartbeat). A killed-empty fleet is still selectable but is NOT \"available\" for path 2.\n\n<!--PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY-->\n\n# Operating brief — this launch\n\n> Generated from the selected scope and plan. The evidence-only judge role is intentionally excluded from coordination-write\\n  tools, so it must not call coord:declare-intent, claim plan lanes, or pass intent to\\n  coord:orient (that causes an internal declaration attempt). Judges may call coord:orient\\n  {} without intent for omitted read context, then work only the item already routed to\\n  them. This omits memory recall and intent declaration by design.\\n\\n  **ROUTE A — an `## Orientation` block already arrived in this turn.** Your held\\n  work-items, unanswered directed messages, and whether a wake source (armed loop)\\n  exists came WITH it: the server read them for you. Do NOT spend a\\n  `coord:orient` round-trip re-fetching them — you are oriented. Claim your lane\\n  with `coord:declare-intent { intent, items }`, and reach for\\n  `coord:orient` only for what that block deliberately EXCLUDES: the claimable\\n  backlog, full inbox bodies, a mem0 recall. Judge by PRESENCE ONLY — the block is\\n  emitted just when that state CHANGES, and only to hosts that inject it, so its\\n  ABSENCE never means \\\"you are oriented\\\".\\n\\n  **ROUTE B — no such block.** Bootstrap in ONE call:\\n  **`coord:orient { intent }`** — pass your one-line intent for the\\n  task. In a SINGLE round-trip it returns your current assignments\\n  (+ lane + load), the claimable backlog, your unread inbox summary,\\n  the recent plan-events delta, AND a mem0 recall for `intent` — and\\n  it DECLARES `intent` to peers so they see what you're working on.\\n  After a SUCCESSFUL orient, do NOT separately call `coord:plan-events`,\\n  `memory:search`, `coord:inbox`, or `coord:declare-intent` — orient's\\n  result ALREADY contains them (plan-events delta + inbox summary + a mem0\\n  recall) and ALREADY declared your intent; re-calling them just re-pays the\\n  round-trip orient collapsed. Reach for one individually only for a detail\\n  orient deliberately bounds (full inbox bodies, or a mem0 query OTHER than\\n  your intent).\\n\\n  - **Claim your lane.** When the work is plan items, pass them:\\n    `coord:orient { intent, planSlug, planItems: ['P-001', …] }` CLAIMS\\n    those items for you (and releases ones you've moved off). An unclaimed\\n    lane is invisible to the Mug and peers, so work gets double-placed.\\n    (Flipping an item `wip` via `plans:set-status` also auto-claims;\\n    `done` releases. A `claim_conflict` means a live peer holds it —\\n    coordinate with the holder, don't take it.)\\n  - **mem0 (what you know).** orient's recall uses `intent` as the query;\\n    pass `harness` for project-specific facts. Each mem0 hit carries an\\n    `id` — if the user later contradicts something, `memory:forget`\\n    that id. Use `memoryQuery` for a different query, or call\\n    `memory:search` directly. A recall hit is BINDING context, not flavor:\\n    if a recalled fact prescribes a behavior for THIS task, follow it — or\\n    explicitly say why you're not.\\n  - **insights (how things work).** When you hit a confusing failure,\\n    `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section before grepping code —\\n    many \\\"weird bugs\\\" already have a written runbook.\\n  - **State answers NOW; only the append-only log answers EVER.** `coord:presence` /\\n    `fleet:assignments` are LIVE-STATE — who is alive, who holds what RIGHT NOW; an ended\\n    agent loses its fleet_slug and its presence row is TTL-reaped, so they CANNOT answer an\\n    *ever / was / missed / history* question. Route those to `coord:catch-up { audience }`\\n    (as a member of the fleet/topic) or `coord:feed { audience }` (the firehose) instead —\\n    never a state tool. Full map:\\n    `docs:search` `agent-insights/presence-vs-history-who-is-on-what`.\\n\\nRight layer for READS and WRITES — the memory↔docs boundary:\\n  - **HOW IT WORKS** (a runbook, a failure mode, why-something-is, a hard-won gotcha):\\n    READ via `docs:search` the `agent-insights/` section; WRITE a new/updated MDX under\\n    `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/` with a `documents:` frontmatter\\n    anchor to the code it describes. This is the RIGHT place — a doc is code-ANCHORED,\\n    drift-TRACKED (the freshness sweep) and AUTO-HEALED (the doc-steward); a mem0 vector cannot\\n    be anchored/swept/auto-rewritten, so how-it-works left only in mem0 silently rots. Do NOT\\n    park a runbook in mem0.\\n  - **WHY a subsystem/decision is the way it is** (the rationale behind a design, not how it works):\\n    READ via `rationale:feed { topic }` — a topic-keyed projection over the relevant\\n    plan-decisions + work-items + insights, kept fresh by the event engine (`topics:list` for the\\n    topic, then `plans:get`/`docs:get` on an entry's `ref` for the full text). The discoverable\\n    \\\"why\\\" layer — reach for it before grepping plans/decisions by hand.\\n  - **A durable PERSONAL/PREFERENCE fact** (who the user is, a convention, an owner pref):\\n    READ via `memory:search`; WRITE via `memory:remember`. Keep mem0 entries SHORT, and when\\n    the why already lives in a doc/plan store only the non-derivable fact + a POINTER\\n    (`[[<plan-slug>]]`, `/internal/docs/agent-insights/<slug>`), never a copied paragraph.\\n  - **In-flight state** → coord; **derivable session state** (X shipped, migration N, N tests)\\n    → the plan / work-item, never memory.\\nSee the plans `papercusp-su-memory-2026-05-25` and\\n`tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21`.\\n\\n## Your tool surface is DYNAMIC — the whole 959-tool catalog is reachable on demand\\n\\nYour loaded tool list is usually a small CORE set (the default). Any tool NOT in it is still\\nreachable — you do not need everything loaded up front:\\n- **`tools:find(\\\"<what you want to do>\\\")`** — intent search; matched tools are activated so you can call them directly next.\\n- **`tools:invoke({ name, args })`** — call ANY tool by exact name without loading it (the universal fallback).\\nWhen you need a capability that isn't in your loaded set, SEARCH for it — don't assume it doesn't exist.\\n⚠ Your CLIENT's own tool search (Claude Code ToolSearch, OMP search_tool_bm25) indexes ONLY this\\nadvertised subset — a zero-hit search THERE does NOT mean the tool doesn't exist (EI-9011: agents\\nhit this and degraded to polling). Use this before building `retireIds` instead of fetching the full checkpoint body.\\n  checksOnly?: boolean;\\n  // also return topics, thread posts (comments), outgoing links, `lifecycle` — the unified history (blocks, holds, reopens) with a coverage report saying what is NOT recorded — and `priorAttempts`, the bounded prior-attempt brief (what was already tried on this item's plan lane, and what the budget OMITTED). Accepts `true`/`false`, or the aliases `'full'`/`'summary'` (some tools in this catalog use that string-enum convention instead).\\n  detail?: boolean;\\n  // caller harness scope; do not copy a cross-hive row's canonical harness here\\n  harness?: string;\\n  // a single work-item id (n=1 shorthand for ids:[id])\\n  id?: string;\\n  // work-item ids to fetch (1–100)\\n  ids?: Array<string>;\\n  // Add `operationalBrief` per row: claim/state, blockers, last verified evidence, next action and successor residue, projected from this same read. Unmeasured fields are explicit `unknown` with a reason, never zero. Forces a complete read; not with resume or checksOnly.\\n  operationalBrief?: boolean;\\n  // raw drill-down for the requested work-item(s): pass `id` (one) or `ids` (many) together with these refs. Resolve refs back to their FULL untruncated source records. When combined with `detail:true`, this replaces the bounded `priorAttempts` brief so the response does not mix clipped history with the raw records; make a separate read if you need both views. Take refs from a brief's `omission.omittedRefs` (records the budget could only COUNT) or from a clipped record's own `rawRef` — the brief names them precisely so a bounded read is never a dead end. Refs that no longer resolve come back in `unresolved[]`, which is an answer about the history, not an error.\\n  priorAttemptRefs?: Array<string>;\\n  // Standalone one-item continuation view: current claim, complete structured next action, saved checks and exact evidence references, with freshness and scoped recovery. Uses checkpoint:{did,left,next} written by work_items:checkpoint; missing/unreadable state remains explicit. Do not combine with detail, checksOnly, threadLimit, priorAttemptRefs, or operationalBrief; use a separate read for those enrichments.\\n  resume?: boolean;\\n  // return a bounded oldest-first recent-comment window instead of loading the full thread; 0 explicitly suppresses thread work, positive values return up to 10 posts with a same-snapshot total. The effective window is capped at 10: a larger value is CLAMPED (not rejected) and the result reports `threadLimitClamped:{requested,applied}` — read `threadWindow.total`, not `shown`, for how many posts exist.\\n  threadLimit?: number;\\n}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };\\n```\"}]"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12354-7a05-7373-9437-3faf5871e1b1","create_time":1791594109.667998}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T01:08:52.557Z","ordinal":239,"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"custom_tool_call","id":"ctc_00adc9e19041eb8c016ac9902331508195ab3d0d6e0c459173","status":"completed","call_id":"call_7bd3ed6959ff456eaec5c675b39bedad","name":"exec","input":"const cmds = [\n  [\"native_route_refs\", \"rg -n -F 'verify-tauri-headless' apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs packages/operator-core apps/operator\"],\n  [\"native_script\", \"sed -n '1,240p' scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh\"],\n  [\"journey_test_refs\", \"rg -n 'OS-restart|resumedEngine|composer|Codex.*Bash|usage|restart' packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts\"],\n  [\"test_file_router\", \"rg -n 'test:file' package.json scripts\"]\n];\nconst results = await Promise.allSettled(cmds.map(async ([key,cmd]) => [key,await tools.exec_command({\n  cmd, workdir:\"/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp\", yield_time_ms:30000, max_output_tokens:3000\n})]));\nfor (const r of results) {\n  if(r.status!==\"fulfilled\"){text({error:String(r.reason)});continue;}\n  let [key,result]=r.value;\n  while(\"session_id\" in result && !(\"exit_code\" in result)) result=await tools.write_stdin({session_id:result.session_id,chars:\"\",yield_time_ms:30000,max_output_tokens:3000});\n  text([key,result]);\n}\n","internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12354-7a05-7373-9437-3faf5871e1b1","create_time":1791594531.193915}}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T01:08:52.800Z","ordinal":241,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a12354-76df-7230-8a3e-7b5bc95a62ef","turn_id":"01a12354-7a05-7373-9437-3faf5871e1b1","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-926f9b67-9267-42f0-982c-617b4c2b77fe","process_id":"49684","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1,240p' scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1,240p' scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh","name":"verify-tauri-headless.sh","path":"scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh — EI-9005.\n#\n# THE PROBLEM: agents verifying Papercusp desktop UI either fight over the\n# owner's live :0 Tauri window (focus-steal, disrupts real fleet work — see\n# apps/operator-docs/.../testing/agent-e2e.mdx §0/§1.3), or, on finding the\n# live window busy/contended, silently skip the owner-required UI-verification\n# gate because hand-deriving an isolated Xvfb+VirtualGL+bridge instance every\n# time (agent-e2e.mdx §1.3 + §15.4) is expensive enough on a loaded box that\n# skipping looks rational. Two independent work-items hit this same gap the\n# same week (EI-9005, WI-3658) — evidence it's recurring, not one-off.\n#\n# THE FIX: package the already-documented isolated-instance recipe as ONE\n# script. Boots a `papercusp-desktop` dev instance with its own devUrl port and\n# its own operator sidecar process, under an isolated Xvfb + VirtualGL X server\n# (real GPU, so screenshots aren't blank — see the GL trap in agent-e2e.mdx\n# §15.4) — waits for its dev-bridge to come up, execs the caller's assertion\n# command against it, then tears the whole process tree + X server down. It\n# NEVER touches DISPLAY :0/:1 (the owner's real desktop) and never sets\n# PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER_WORKERS (the WI-3556 shadow trap documented in\n# agent-e2e.mdx §1.3 — the wrapper script already pins PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=0 for\n# exactly this reason; setting CLUSTER_WORKERS ourselves would silently shadow\n# that safety pin).\n#\n# EI-20200818150345989: a bridge PID discovered by `tauri-agent-tools probe` is\n# not proof that it belongs to an agent. The owner's live desktop can expose a\n# healthy bridge on the same box, and driving it is destructive. Every verifier\n# launched from a tracked su session therefore carries both the existing\n# PAPERCUSP_SID and a dedicated launch-provenance marker. The bridge handoff\n# below matches both markers from the target process's own /proc environ before\n# exporting VERIFY_TAURI_PID; an unowned or owner-launched bridge is never handed\n# to the assertion command.\n#\n# ⚠️  WHAT IS **NOT** ISOLATED — READ THIS BEFORE YOU CLICK ANYTHING (EI-10387)\n#\n#   ISOLATED:      the X display, the devUrl port, the pty port, the sidecar\n#                  *process*, and (EI-10364) the SPA MODULE BUNDLE — a frozen\n#                  snapshot the fleet's shared `vite build --watch` can't touch,\n#                  so this webview's module graph is stable for the whole run.\n#   **NOT** ISOLATED: the DATABASE, the WORKSPACE, and the WebView profile. The\n#                  sidecar inherits the ambient env, so it connects to the SAME\n#                  `DATABASE_URL` / `PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE` as the live system, and\n#                  WebKit localStorage belongs to the desktop's normal profile.\n#\n#   => **EVERY WRITE YOU MAKE IN THIS WINDOW IS A REAL WRITE TO LIVE STATE.**\n#      Clicking a Mug steering control here mutates the owner's real steering\n#      AND calls requestUrgentHiveWake() — waking the real Mug and burning real\n#      tokens. Toggling a routine here really toggles it (git-sync included).\n#\n#   This header used to claim \"own embedded-PG, own workspace state; NOT just a\n#   second window pointed at shared backend state\". That was FALSE, and it is\n#   exactly the kind of claim an agent takes on trust before clicking a\n#   destructive button — so it was corrected here rather than left to mislead.\n#\n#   EI-10387 (2026-07-18): the claim is now TRUE, OPT-IN. Pass\n#   VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1 and this script boots a throwaway, fully-migrated,\n#   per-run embedded Postgres (own datadir, own free port — nobody else's pot),\n#   scopes PAPERCUSP_HOME/PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE and the Tauri WebView data/cache\n#   profile to this run, and *asserts at boot*\n#   (reading the real sidecar process's own /proc/<pid>/environ, not just our own\n#   env construction) that the resolved DB actually differs from the live one —\n#   refusing to proceed otherwise. Every write in that mode is safe: it lands in\n#   the throwaway DB, which nothing else reads, and is discarded at teardown. The\n#   instance boots into the normal first-run onboarding flow (an empty, freshly-\n#   migrated DB — the same state every real fresh install boots into), not the\n#   owner's real pots/plans. One wrong flag name burns a full verifier cycle.</p>\\n\"}]\n[\"native_script\",{\"chunk_id\":\"1764b7\",\"wall_time_seconds\":0.000033775,\"exit_code\":0,\"original_token_count\":4022,\"output\":\"Warning: truncated output (original token count: 4022)\\nTotal output lines: 240\\n\\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\\n# scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh — EI-9005.\\n#\\n# THE PROBLEM: agents verifying Papercusp desktop UI either fight over the\\n# owner's live :0 Tauri window (focus-steal, disrupts real fleet work — see\\n# apps/operator-docs/.../testing/agent-e2e.mdx §0/§1.3), or, on finding the\\n# live window busy/contended, silently skip the owner-required UI-verification\\n# gate because hand-deriving an isolated Xvfb+VirtualGL+bridge instance every\\n# time (agent-e2e.mdx §1.3 + §15.4) is expensive enough on a loaded box that\\n# skipping looks rational. Two independent work-items hit this same gap the\\n# same week (EI-9005, WI-3658) — evidence it's recurring, not one-off.\\n#\\n# THE FIX: package the already-documented isolated-instance recipe as ONE\\n# script. Boots a `papercusp-desktop` dev instance with its own devUrl port and\\n# its own operator sidecar process, under an isolated Xvfb + VirtualGL X server\\n# (real GPU, so screenshots aren't blank — see the GL trap in agent-e2e.mdx\\n# §15.4) — waits for its dev-bridge to come up, execs the caller's assertion\\n# command against it, then tears the whole process tree + X server down. It\\n# NEVER touches DISPLAY :0/:1 (the owner's real desktop) and never sets\\n# PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER_WORKERS (the WI-3556 shadow trap documented in\\n# agent-e2e.mdx §1.3 — the wrapper script already pins PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=0 for\\n# exactly this reason; setting CLUSTER_WORKERS ourselves would silently shadow\\n# that safety pin).\\n#\\n# EI-20200818150345989: a bridge PID discovered by `tauri-agent-tools probe` is\\n# not proof that it belongs to an agent. The owner's live desktop can expose a\\n# healthy bridge on the same box, and driving it is destructive. Every verifier\\n# launched from a tracked su session therefore carries both the existing\\n# PAPERCUSP_SID and a dedicated launch-provenance marker. The bridge handoff\\n# below matches both markers from the target process's own /proc environ before\\n# exporting VERIFY_TAURI_PID; an unowned or owner-launched bridge is never handed\\n# to the assertion command.\\n#\\n# ⚠️  WHAT IS **NOT** ISOLATED — READ THIS BEFORE YOU CLICK ANYTHING (EI-10387)\\n#\\n#   ISOLATED:      the X display, the devUrl port, the pty port, the sidecar\\n#                  *process*, and (EI-10364) the SPA MODULE BUNDLE — a frozen\\n#                  snapshot the fleet's shared `vite build --watch` can't touch,\\n#                  so this webview's module graph is stable for the whole run.\\n#   **NOT** ISOLATED: the DATABASE, the WORKSPACE, and the WebView profile. Example:\n#       scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh -- bash -c \"\n#         tauri-agent-tools eval --pid \\\"\\$VERIFY_TAURI_PID\\\" \\\n#           'window.__TSR_ROUTER__?.navigate({ to: \\\"/settings/p2p\\\" })'\n#         \\\"\\$VERIFY_TAURI_POLL\\\" --selector body --text Peer --no-errors\n#       \"\n#     The outer double-quoted script deliberately escapes its variables and\n#     keeps the JS expression in single quotes. A nested bash -c with an\n#     unescaped double-quoted JS argument strips the route/selector quotes\n#     before tauri-agent-tools sees them, producing an invalid assertion.\n#     VERIFY_TAURI_POLL retries a data-dependent DOM assertion after navigation\n#     (bounded by VERIFY_TAURI_DOM_TIMEOUT) instead of racing it with a fixed sleep.\n#     GUARD EVERY NEGATIVE ASSERTION (EI-18781011720418569). \"the old copy is\n#     gone\" / \"no undefined leaked\" / \"no error banner\" are all trivially TRUE of\n#     an empty document, so they pass before the sync-backed rows have arrived —\n#     a green exit that verified nothing. Name the subject that must be present:\n#       \\\"\\$VERIFY_TAURI_POLL\\\" --require '[data-testid=\\\"schedule-row\\\"]' \\\n#         --eval '!document.body.innerHTML.includes(\\\"paused from its own subsystem\\\")'\n#     The guard is fused into the SAME evaluation (add --require-min N when one\n#     node is not enough), so nothing can slip between \"rows present\" and\n#     \"string absent\". An unguarded negative --eval is REFUSED, not run; the\n#     escape hatch --allow-unguarded-negative is only for a subject an EARLIER\n#     assertion in the same run already proved renders.\n#     `tauri-agent-tools eval` pretty-prints object results, even when the JS\n#     expression returns JSON.stringify(...). If a shell probe must inspect an\n#     eval result, allow the formatting whitespace:\n#       R=\"$(tauri-agent-tools eval --pid \\\"$VERIFY_TAURI_PID\\\" \\\n#         'JSON.stringify({ok: !!document.querySelector(\\\"...\\\")})')\"\n#       grep -qE '\"ok\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true' <<<\"$R\"\n#     Prefer VERIFY_TAURI_POLL (or `tauri-agent-tools check --json`) for DOM\n#     assertions; a literal `grep '\"ok\":true'` never matches pretty-printed\n#     output because the property/value separator includes a space.\n#     WAIT BEFORE YOU MEASURE (EI-19385008818210514). VERIFY_TAURI_POLL retries\n#     an ASSERTION until it succeeds; it does nothing for a MEASUREMENT whose\n#     value you then read as data:\n#       zoneCaps: 2, zoneCapLabels: [\"Controls\", \"Fleet\"]\n#     Three were expected. That reads as unfinished work — and it was a race.\n#     Most components here are guarded on async data (`entry && <Thing/>`,\n#     `if (!x) return null`), so before the data lands they are legitimately\n#     absent, and the wrong conclusion (\"the feature was never implemented\")\n#     is confident, plausible and only ever fires against finished work.\n#     Settle first, then measure:\n#       bash \\\"\\$VERIFY_TAURI_SETTLE\\\"\n#       tauri-agent-tools eval --pid \\\"\\$VERIFY_TAURI_PID\\\" '<your measurement>'\n#     VERIFY_TAURI_SETTLE blocks until the sync transport is idle AND the DOM has\n#     stopped mutating. It is THREE-state: exit 0 settled, 1 still busy at\n#     timeout, 3 UNKNOWN (window.__sync_metrics__ absent, or the gate reported\n#     null — which means \"no gate registered\", never \"zero in flight\"). An\n#     UNKNOWN is not permission to conclude anything from an absence.\n#     You do not have to remember any of this: the same probe runs in\n#     --note-only form on every VERIFY_TAURI_POLL timeout, and prints the\n#     loading context (and nothing at all when the page really was settled).\n#\n#   scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh --boot-only\n#     Boots the instance, prints one source command for a private mode-600\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":37823}},"started_at_ms":1791594545317,"completed_at_ms":1791594545317}}

A nested bash -c with an\\n#     unescaped double-quoted JS argument strips the route/selector quotes\\n#     before tauri-agent-tools sees them, producing an invalid assertion.\\n#     VERIFY_TAURI_POLL retries a data-dependent DOM assertion after navigation\\n#     (bounded by VERIFY_TAURI_DOM_TIMEOUT) instead of racing it with a fixed sleep.\\n#     GUARD EVERY NEGATIVE ASSERTION (EI-18781011720418569). \\\"the old copy is\\n#     gone\\\" / \\\"no undefined leaked\\\" / \\\"no error banner\\\" are all trivially TRUE of\\n#     an empty document, so they pass before the sync-backed rows have arrived —\\n#     a green exit that verified nothing. Name the subject that must be present:\\n#       \\\\\\\"\\\\$VERIFY_TAURI_POLL\\\\\\\" --require '[data-testid=\\\\\\\"schedule-row\\\\\\\"]' \\\\\\n#         --eval '!document.body.innerHTML.includes(\\\\\\\"paused from its own subsystem\\\\\\\")'\\n#     The guard is fused into the SAME evaluation (add --require-min N when one\\n#     node is not enough), so nothing can slip between \\\"rows present\\\" and\\n#     \\\"string absent\\\". If a shell probe must inspect an\\n#     eval result, allow the formatting whitespace:\\n#       R=\\\"$(tauri-agent-tools eval --pid \\\\\\\"$VERIFY_TAURI_PID\\\\\\\" \\\\\\n#         'JSON.stringify({ok: !!document.querySelector(\\\\\\\"...\\\\\\\")})')\\\"\\n#       grep -qE '\\\"ok\\\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true' <<<\\\"$R\\\"\\n#     Prefer VERIFY_TAURI_POLL (or `tauri-agent-tools check --json`) for DOM\\n#     assertions; a literal `grep '\\\"ok\\\":true'` never matches pretty-printed\\n#     output because the property/value separator includes a space.\\n#     WAIT BEFORE YOU MEASURE (EI-19385008818210514). Live-verified 2026-07-10 (isolated bridge PID resolved distinct\\nfrom the live fleet's own bridge; DOM check passed; clean teardown, no\\norphaned processes or display).\\n\\n```sh\\nscripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh -- bash -c '\\n  tauri-agent-tools check --pid \\\"$VERIFY_TAURI_PID\\\" \\\\\\n    --selector body --no-errors'\\n```\\n\\n`scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh --boot-only` prints one source command for a\\nprivate, mode-600 per-run env file plus a stop script for a multi-step\\ninteractive session. Run that command in the same tracked agent shell that\\nstarted the rig; sourcing the file re-checks the caller's `PAPERCUSP_SID` and\\nthe bridge's own `/proc/<pid>/environ` (`PAPERCUSP_SID`, display, port, and\\nlaunch provenance) before exporting any drive variables. A copied or stale env\\nfile fails closed with `VERIFY_TAURI_ENV_FILE points at a verifier owned by\\nanother session`. Do not redirect raw export blocks from `--boot-only` into a\\nshared log or source a log tail; the handoff is intentionally source-only.\\n\\n:::tip[Multi-step drives are now watcher-proof (EI-10364, closing EI-10360)]\\nOn a busy tree, a bare isolated instance used to reuse the SHARED\\n`apps/operator-vite/dist/` module server — the exact bundle the fleet's\\n`vite build --watch` continuously rewrites/empties. Any peer's operator-vite\\nedit could invalidate an already-open page's lazy chunks mid-drive\\n(`Importing a module script failed`), turning a multi-step\\nnavigate→click→assert→click→assert sequence into a coin-flip.\\n\\n`scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh` now **freezes a private per-run snapshot**\\nof the shared dist (`PAPERCUSP_SPA_DIST`) before boot, so this instance's\\nmodule graph is immutable for the whole run — a peer's concurrent edit can no\\nlonger touch it. The script logs `SPA snapshot frozen at … — IMMUTABLE for\\nthis run; restart to pick up a newer build.` when it engages.\\n\\n**The snapshot is immutable — it never re-reads the source after boot, and\\nthere is no ambient warning for that (EI-17134).** If you boot a `--boot-only`\\n```\\n\\nSilent + exit 0 = nothing changed since boot, the snapshot is still current.\\nA loud warning + exit 1 = the shared dist changed after this instance froze —\\nrestart (`\\\"$VERIFY_TAURI_STOP\\\"` then re-run the boot script) before trusting\\nany further checks; reloading the page will NOT pick up the edit.\\n\\n### Assertion (`--`) mode runs that guard FOR you — and can settle it decisively\\n\\nThe above is the `--boot-only` workflow, where *you* drive an instance and so\\n*you* must remember to check. In assertion mode\\n(`verify-tauri-headless.sh -- <cmd>`) the script now runs the freshness check\\nitself, just before exec'ing your command — you no longer have to remember it.\\n(`$VERIFY_TAURI_FRESHNESS_CHECK` used to be exported **only** on the\\n`--boot-only` path, so referencing it from an assertion command died with\\n`VERIFY_TAURI_FRESHNESS_CHECK: unbound variable` — EI-19444780917356384. It and\\n`$VERIFY_TAURI_SPA_DIST`, the frozen bundle's path, are now exported in both\\nmodes.)\\n\\nTwo checks fire there, deliberately different in force — and the distinction\\nmatters, because only one of them can actually answer your question:\\n\\n- **Drift (advisory).** \\\"The shared dist moved since we froze.\\\" On this box the\\n  fleet's `vite build --watch` rebuilds constantly, so drift is near-permanent\\n  and does **not** prove *your* change is missing — a peer's unrelated edit\\n  moves it too. It warns and points at the decisive check rather than failing\\n  your run.\\n- **Containment (decisive).** Pass a string your change introduced:\\n\\n  ```bash\\n  VERIFY_TAURI_ASSERT_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINS='myNewSymbol' \\\\\\n    bash scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh -- bash my-assertions.sh\\n  ```\\n\\n  The script greps the **frozen** bundle and, if the string is absent, exits\\n  **3** *before running your command at all* — because a run that cannot\\n\"}]"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a12354-7a05-7373-9437-3faf5871e1b1","create_time":1791594545.8353915}},"metadata":{"client_authored":false,"fallback_token_limit_override":12000}}

{"timestamp":"2026-10-10T01:12:22.366Z","ordinal":382,"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"item_completed","thread_id":"01a12354-76df-7230-8a3e-7b5bc95a62ef","turn_id":"01a12354-7a05-7373-9437-3faf5871e1b1","item":{"type":"CommandExecution","id":"exec-7477317a-a7f5-4ee6-a384-f1811531866b","process_id":"71198","command":["/bin/bash","-lc","sed -n '1,220p' apps/tui/scripts/release-acceptance.sh"],"cwd":"file:///home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp","parsed_cmd":[{"type":"read","cmd":"sed -n '1,220p' apps/tui/scripts/release-acceptance.sh","name":"release-acceptance.sh","path":"apps/tui/scripts/release-acceptance.sh"}],"source":"unified_exec_startup","status":"completed","aggregated_output":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# The installed-TUI release stage (pui-first-party-public-release P-012 / D-018).\n#\n# Installs one candidate archive from apps/tui/scripts/package-release.sh into a\n# clean HOME, drives the production-operator PTY suites through that installed\n# bin/pui, and writes <archive>.acceptance.json. An archive may be published\n# (P-014/P-015) only with a passing acceptance file for the same digest.\n#\n# Isolation (EI-24692155752067316). The stage runs tsx, vitest, the suites and\n# the operator fixture from the checkout it executes in. Run from the shared\n# working tree, a peer's half-written edit lands in the run: rehearsal\n# 37bc2d4c32 lost its claude leg to a transient scripts/next-migration.js and\n# its omp leg to a mid-edit syntax error in gateway.ts, neither of them PUI code.\n# So this script checks out the archive's own source commit (PROVENANCE.json\n# source.commit) with the release checkout helper, object-sourced and with\n# node_modules captured under the maintained install-reader lock into an\n# independent immutable generation, and runs\n# the stage from there. Up to three reusable\n# checkouts live under PUI_ACCEPTANCE_CHECKOUT_ROOT (default\n# ~/.cache/pui-acceptance-checkouts) and are re-pinned on each use.\n# PUI_ACCEPTANCE_ALLOW_LIVE_TREE=1 runs in place instead, for development only:\n# the verdict then refuses (release-acceptance-run.ts runnerTreeRefusals).\n#\n# Exit 0 = accepted, 1 = refused (the file names every reason), 2 = could not run.\n# --help prints the options. Setup output goes to stderr; stdout carries only\n# the stage's own PUI_RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE line.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/../../..\" && pwd)\"\nrun_in() {\n  local root=\"$1\"; shift\n  exec \"$root/node_modules/.bin/tsx\" \"$root/packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/release-acceptance-cli.mts\" \"$@\"\n}\nfail() { echo \"release-acceptance: ERROR: $*\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\narchive=\"\"\nargs=(\"$@\")\nfor ((i = 0; i < ${#args[@]}; i++)); do\n  case \"${args[i]}\" in\n    --archive) archive=\"${args[i + 1]:-}\" ;;\n    --archive=*) archive=\"${args[i]#--archive=}\" ;;\n    -h|--help) run_in \"$ROOT\" \"$@\" ;;\n  esac\ndone\n# No archive: the CLI prints its usage. Already re-executed, or opted out: run here.\nif [ -z \"$archive\" ] || [ -n \"${PUI_ACCEPTANCE_ISOLATED:-}\" ] || [ \"${PUI_ACCEPTANCE_ALLOW_LIVE_TREE:-}\" = 1 ]; then\n  run_in \"$ROOT\" \"$@\"\nfi\n\n[ -f \"$archive\" ] || fail \"no archive at $archive\"\nprovenance=\"$(tar -xzOf \"$archive\" --wildcards --no-wildcards-match-slash '*/PROVENANCE.json')\" \\\n  || fail \"$archive carries no top-level PROVENANCE.json\"\nsha=\"$(printf '%s' \"$provenance\" | node -e '\n  let text = \"\";\n  process.stdin.on(\"data\", (chunk) => { text += chunk; }).on(\"end\", () => {\n    const commit = JSON.parse(text).source?.commit ?? \"\";\n    if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(commit)) process.exit(1);\n    process.stdout.write(commit);\n  });')\" || fail \"$archive PROVENANCE.json has no 40-hex source.commit\"\n\ncheckouts=\"${PUI_ACCEPTANCE_CHECKOUT_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/pui-acceptance-checkouts}\"\nmkdir -p \"$checkouts\"\ncheckouts=\"$(cd \"$checkouts\" && pwd -P)\"\n# A few reusable slots, each re-pinned per run: bounded disk, and a re-pin moves\n# only what changed. One run per slot, since a second would re-pin the tree\n# under the first. The lock is held by this process and everything it execs; a\n# leftover child of an earlier run holds it too (`fuser -v <slot>.lock`).\ncheckout=\"\"\nfor slot in 1 2 3; do\n  exec 9>\"$checkouts/slot-$slot.lock\"\n  if flock -n 9; then checkout=\"$checkouts/slot-$slot\"; break; fi\n  exec 9>&-\ndone\n[ -n \"$checkout\" ] || fail \"all three acceptance checkouts under $checkouts are held by other runs\"\n\necho \"release-acceptance: checking out candidate source $sha at $checkout\" >&2\n# Freeze the shared helper and its adjacent sidecars before its long checkout\n# work. Each slot\n# consumes a validated donor while the shared integration tree may change.\n# Use the maintained install-reader boundary throughout capture/materialization.\nnode \"$ROOT/scripts/npm-install-safe.mjs\" --repo-root \"$ROOT\" --exec-under-lock -- \\\n  bash \"$ROOT/apps/operator/scripts/systemd/papercusp-script-snapshot.sh\" \\\n  \"$ROOT/apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh\" \\\n  --ref \"$sha\" --integration \"$ROOT\" --release \"$checkout\" \\\n  --node-modules force --node-modules-copy copy --node-modules-generation required \\\n  --dependency-generation-root \"$checkouts/dependency-generations\" \\\n  --source-integrity object-sourced >&2 \\\n  || fail \"could not check out $sha at $checkout (setup-release-checkout.sh failed; output above)\"\nlanded=\"$(git -C \"$checkout\" rev-parse HEAD)\"\n[ \"$landed\" = \"$sha\" ] || fail \"checkout $checkout is at $landed, not the candidate source $sha\"\n\nexport PUI_ACCEPTANCE_ISOLATED=\"$checkout\"\nrun_in \"$checkout\" \"$@\"\n","exit_code":0,"duration":{"secs":0,"nanos":25900}},"started_at_ms":1791594742365,"completed_at_ms":1791594742365}}

Without\n * it each leg resolves the fleet's shared, reused Docker test-PG container,\n * which can be recreated between legs: rehearsal 0f06f9d5d6 lost every omp test\n * to `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:32785` after the claude leg had passed on the same\n * container. Docker container creation also stalls on this host\n * (WI-10003403). Host PG binaries need neither. A caller that already set\n * PAPERCUSP_TEST_PG_ADMIN_URL keeps its own server.\n */\nasync function startAcceptancePg(work: string): Promise<{ env: Record<string, string>; stop(): Promise<void> }> {\n  if (process.env.PAPERCUSP_TEST_PG_ADMIN_URL) return { env: {}, stop: async () => {} };\n  const pg = await startDedicatedNativePg({\n    baseDir: work,\n    settings: {\n      max_connections: '500',\n      fsync: 'off',\n      synchronous_commit: 'off',\n      full_page_writes: 'off',\n      // Keep PostgreSQL logs in the collector so they do not interleave with\n      // the acceptance leg's live stdout/stderr log.\n      logging_collector: 'on',\n    },\n  });\n  return { env: { PAPERCUSP_TEST_PG_ADMIN_URL: pg.getConnectionUri() }, stop: () => pg.stop() };\n}\n\nexport const RELEASE_SUITES = [\n  'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts',\n  'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/context-pane-cockpit-pty.integration.test.ts',\n];\n/** The code that decides what counts; it must be the candidate's own copy. */\nconst ACCEPTANCE_SOURCES = [\n  ...RELEASE_SUITES,\n  'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/release-acceptance.ts',\n  'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/release-acceptance-reporter.ts',\n  'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/release-acceptance-run.ts',\n];\nconst REPORTER = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/release-acceptance-reporter.ts');\nconst VITEST = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'node_modules/.bin/vitest');\n// CLI reporter options replace the config's reporter list. Preserve the existing\n// ledger recorder alongside the installed-product evidence collector.\nexport const RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE_REPORTER_ARGS = [\n  '--reporter=default',\n  `--reporter=${ADMIN_TEST_RUNS_REPORTER_PATH}`,\n  `--reporter=${REPORTER}`,\n];\nconst OPERATOR_CORE = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'packages/operator-core');\n\nexport interface LoggedChildResult {\n  status: number | null;\n  signal: NodeJS.Signals | null;\n  error: Error | null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run a child with stdout and stderr sent directly to a live log file. The file\n * is created before spawn and the child inherits its descriptor, so long test\n * legs remain observable while they run instead of only after exit.\n */\nexport function runChildWithLiveLog(\n  command: string,\n  args: string[],\n  options: SpawnOptions,\n  logPath: string,\n): Promise<LoggedChildResult> {\n  writeFileSync(logPath, `--- live child output started ${new Date().toISOString()} ---\\n`);\n  const logFd = openSync(logPath, 'a');\n  let child: ReturnType<typeof spawn>;\n  try {\n    child = spawn(command, args, { ...options, stdio: ['ignore', logFd, logFd] });\n  } catch (caught) {\n    closeSync(logFd);\n    const error = caught instanceof Error ? caught : new Error(String(caught));\n    appendFileSync(logPath, `\\n--- child spawn error: ${error.message} ---\\n`);\n    return Promise.resolve({ status: null, signal: null, error });\n  }\n  closeSync(logFd);\n\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    let processError: Error | null = null;\n    child.once('error', (error) => { processError = error; });\n    child.once('close', (status, signal) => {\n      try {\n        appendFileSync(logPath,\n          `\\n--- child exit: code=${status ?? 'null'} signal=${signal ?? 'none'}${processError ? ` error=${processError.message}` : ''} ---\\n`);\n        resolve({ status, signal, error: processError });\n      } catch (error) {\n        reject(error);\n      }\n    });\n  });\n}\n\nexport interface RealLeg {\n  /** PUI_REAL_BACKEND: claude | codex | omp. */\n  backend: string;\n  /** Pinned per D-012; omitted only where D-013 refuses a pin (OMP under account=auto). */\n  model?: string;\n  env?: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nexport interface RunOptions {\n  archive: string;\n  advertise: Array<{ platform: string; backend: string }>;\n  real?: RealLeg[];\n  /** Vitest -t pattern; the full release run leaves it unset. */\n  testFilter?: string;\n  suites?: string[];\n  out?: string;\n  work?: string;\n  /** Test seam: the platform this run's evidence is recorded against. */\n  platform?: string;\n}\n\nexport interface RunResult {\n  verdict: Verdict;\n  out: string;\n  legs: Array<{ engine: string; status: number | null; evidence: string; rows: number }>;\n  stockMachines: StockMachineResult[];\n  cloudDeviceStart: CloudDeviceStartResult;\n  suiteProvenance: Array<{ file: string; candidateBlob: string | null; runBlob: string | null }>;\n  runnerTree: { before: RunnerTree; after: RunnerTree };\n}\n\nexport interface StockMachineResult {\n  image: string;\n  /**\n   * True when the host could not start a container at all (the create/start\n   * preflight refused), so the image never ran the candidate.
